Simulated panel with a factor structure

Source: R/simulate.R
trop_simulate.Rd

trop_simulate() makes a balanced panel with unit effects, time effects, a low-rank interactive term, and Gaussian noise. Each unit gets a score, which is selection times its first factor loading plus random noise. The units with the highest scores get the treatment.

With a positive value of selection, a unit with a larger loading has a higher probability of treatment. With a negative value, a unit with a smaller loading has a higher probability. With zero, the loading has no effect on the selection. Imputation with two-way fixed effects (TWFE imputation) does not model this factor, so its estimate for one panel can have a large error. TROP can reduce such errors, but some error can stay.

Usage

trop_simulate(
  n_units = 40L,
  n_periods = 30L,
  n_treated = 8L,
  n_post = 5L,
  effect = 1,
  rank = 2L,
  sigma = 0.5,
  selection = 1,
  design = c("block", "staggered"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n_units, n_periods

The number of units and the number of periods.

n_treated

The number of treated units.

n_post

For a block design, the number of treated periods at the end of the panel. For a staggered design, the treatment starts in one of the last n_post periods.

effect

The constant treatment effect on each treated cell.

rank

The rank of the interactive term.

sigma

The standard deviation of the noise.

selection

The weight of the first factor loading in the selection of the treated units. With zero, the selection is random.

design

Use "block" or "staggered".

seed

An optional seed. The function does not change the state of the random number generator in the R session.

Value

A data frame with the columns unit, time, y, d, and y0. The column y0 contains the outcome without the treatment.

Examples

head(trop_simulate(seed = 1))
#>   unit time          y d         y0
#> 1    1    1  0.2388666 0  0.2388666
#> 2    2    1  0.5934588 0  0.5934588
#> 3    3    1 -2.5737706 0 -2.5737706
#> 4    4    1  1.2415187 0  1.2415187
#> 5    5    1  0.4650530 0  0.4650530
#> 6    6    1  0.5049260 0  0.5049260
